Supply Chain Wave 2

GlassWorm Returns: Open VSX Extensions Compromised in Second Wave Supply Chain Attack

February 3, 2026 16 min read TheHGTech Security Research

The self-propagating GlassWorm malware has struck again, this time compromising established Open VSX extensions through credential theft. The new variant targets macOS developers and uses blockchain infrastructure for command-and-control. 

        <img src="/images/articles/glassworm-openvsx-supply-chain-2026.png" alt="GlassWorm Open VSX Attack"
            class="featured-image" loading="lazy">

        <!-- Executive Summary -->
        <div class="warning-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Executive Summary</strong>
            <ul style="margin-top: 1rem;">
                <li><strong>What:</strong> Second wave of GlassWorm malware targeting VS Code extensions</li>
                <li><strong>Target:</strong> Open VSX Registry (alternative to Microsoft Marketplace)</li>
                <li><strong>Affected:</strong> 4 extensions from developer "oorzc" — 22,000+ downloads</li>
                <li><strong>Vector:</strong> Compromised publishing credentials (leaked token)</li>
                <li><strong>Platform:</strong> Primarily macOS — steals credentials, crypto wallets, documents</li>
                <li><strong>C2:</strong> Solana blockchain + Google Calendar fallback ("EtherHiding")</li>
                <li><strong>Status:</strong> Malicious versions removed; users should update immediately</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h2 id="background"><i class="fas fa-history"></i> Background: The GlassWorm Saga</h2>

        <p>
            GlassWorm first emerged in <strong>October 2025</strong> when Koi Security researchers identified
            malicious extensions in both the Open VSX Registry and Microsoft's VS Code Marketplace. That initial
            wave compromised 8 extensions with approximately 36,000 downloads.
        </p>

        <p>
            What made GlassWorm particularly concerning was its <strong>self-propagating capability</strong>:
            the malware was designed to steal developer credentials from platforms like npm, GitHub, and Open VSX
            itself, enabling attackers to spread to additional packages and extensions.
        </p>

        <div class="info-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-link"></i> Related Coverage</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem;">
                For developers concerned about IDE security, see our comprehensive guide:
                <a href="/guides/vscode-supply-chain-hardening-2026.html">Securing the AI-Powered IDE: VS Code,
                    Cursor & Windsurf Hardening</a>
            </p>
        </div>

        <h2 id="wave2"><i class="fas fa-wave-square"></i> Wave 2: The January 2026 Attack</h2>

        <p>
            On <strong>January 30, 2026</strong>, security researchers detected malicious updates pushed to four
            established Open VSX extensions from developer <strong>"oorzc"</strong>. Unlike the first wave where
            attackers created new malicious extensions, this attack targeted <em>existing, trusted extensions</em>.
        </p>

        <h3>Compromised Extensions</h3>

        <div class="extension-card">
            <span class="ext-name">vscode-json-transform</span>
            <span class="ext-downloads">| 8,200+ downloads | Active since 2024</span>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0; color: var(--text-secondary);">JSON manipulation utilities for VS Code</p>
        </div>

        <div class="extension-card">
            <span class="ext-name">markdown-preview-enhanced-plus</span>
            <span class="ext-downloads">| 6,100+ downloads | Active since 2023</span>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0; color: var(--text-secondary);">Enhanced Markdown preview features</p>
        </div>

        <div class="extension-card">
            <span class="ext-name">code-snippets-manager</span>
            <span class="ext-downloads">| 4,800+ downloads | Active since 2024</span>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0; color: var(--text-secondary);">Personal code snippet organization tool</p>
        </div>

        <div class="extension-card">
            <span class="ext-name">terminal-themes-collection</span>
            <span class="ext-downloads">| 2,900+ downloads | Active since 2024</span>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0; color: var(--text-secondary);">Custom terminal color schemes</p>
        </div>

        <h3>Attack Vector: Credential Compromise</h3>
        <p>
            The attack was enabled by <strong>compromised publishing credentials</strong>. Evidence suggests the
            developer's Open VSX token was either leaked or stolen, allowing attackers to push malicious updates
            through the legitimate update mechanism.
        </p>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Possible Compromise Vector</th>
                    <th>Likelihood</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>Hardcoded token in public repository</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-orange);">High</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Phishing attack on developer</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-orange);">High</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Token stolen from previous GlassWorm infection</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-red);">Very High</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Insider threat</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-green);">Low</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h2 id="technical"><i class="fas fa-microscope"></i> Technical Analysis</h2>

        <h3>Infection Chain</h3>

        <div class="ascii-diagram">
            <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

GLASSWORM WAVE 2 INFECTION CHAIN

┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ OPEN VSX │────▶│ EXTENSION │────▶│ DEVELOPER │ │ REGISTRY │ │ UPDATE │ │ WORKSTATION │ │ │ │ (Malicious) │ │ (macOS) │ └─────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ │ GLASSWORM │ │ LOADER │ │ (extension.js) │ └──────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ CREDENTIAL │ │ CRYPTO │ │ PERSISTENCE │ │ THEFT │ │ WALLET │ │ + SOCKS │ │ │ │ THEFT │ │ │ │ • SSH Keys │ │ • MetaMask │ │ • LaunchAgent│ │ • AWS Creds │ │ • Phantom │ │ • SOCKS Proxy│ │ • npm Tokens │ │ • Ledger │ │ • Hidden VNC │ │ • GitHub PAT │ │ • Keychain │ │ │ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ │ C2 EXFIL │ │ (Solana Chain) │ └──────────────────┘ 

        <h3>Unicode Steganography: Invisible Malicious Code</h3>
        <p>
            GlassWorm employs <strong>Unicode variation selectors</strong> to hide malicious code within seemingly
            legitimate extension files. These invisible characters are imperceptible in code editors but execute
            when the extension loads.
        </p>

        <div class="technical-box">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-eye-slash"></i> Hidden Code Example</h3>
            <pre><code class="language-javascript">// This looks innocent, but contains hidden payload

const message = “Hello, World!”; console.log(message); // ︀︁︂︃︄︅︆︇︈︉︊︋︌ ← Invisible variation selectors (U+FE00-U+FE0F) // These decode to: eval(atob(“bWFsaWNpb3VzQ29kZSgp”))

The line above the comment contains invisible Unicode characters that encode a malicious payload. 

        <h3>Blockchain C2: EtherHiding Technique</h3>
        <p>
            The January 2026 variant uses the <strong>EtherHiding</strong> technique—storing C2 configuration
            in Solana blockchain transactions. This makes takedowns nearly impossible since blockchain data is
            immutable and decentralized.
        </p>

        <div class="blockchain-highlight">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-cubes"></i> Solana C2 Mechanism</h3>
            <ol>
                <li>Malware queries a specific Solana wallet address</li>
                <li>Retrieves transaction memo fields containing encoded C2 addresses</li>
                <li>Decodes memo to get current active C2 server</li>
                <li>Falls back to Google Calendar events if blockchain fails</li>
            </ol>
            <p style="margin-top: 1rem; color: var(--text-secondary);">
                <strong>Implication:</strong> Attackers can update C2 infrastructure without modifying the malware,
                and defenders cannot simply block a domain—the entire Solana RPC endpoint would need to be blocked.
            </p>
        </div>

        <div class="technical-box">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-code"></i> Solana C2 Fetcher (Deobfuscated)</h3>
            <pre><code class="language-javascript">async function getC2Address() {
const WALLET = "7xF9...vQp3"; // Attacker-controlled wallet
const RPC = "https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com";

try {
    // Fetch recent transactions
    const response = await fetch(RPC, {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({
            jsonrpc: "2.0",
            id: 1,
            method: "getSignaturesForAddress",
            params: [WALLET, { limit: 1 }]
        })
    });
    
    const txData = await response.json();
    const txSignature = txData.result[0].signature;
    
    // Get transaction details (contains C2 in memo)
    const txDetails = await getTransaction(txSignature);
    const memo = decodeMessage(txDetails.transaction.message);
    
    // Decode base64 memo to get C2 address
    return atob(memo); // Returns: "wss://c2-server.attacker[.]com"
} catch (e) {
    // Fallback to Google Calendar
    return await getC2FromCalendar();
}

} 

        <h3>macOS-Specific Targeting</h3>
        <p>
            The January 2026 variant specifically targets <strong>macOS developers</strong>. Stolen data includes:
        </p>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Data Type</th>
                    <th>Location</th>
                    <th>Risk</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>SSH Keys</td>
                    <td>~/.ssh/</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-red);">Critical — Access to servers</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>AWS Credentials</td>
                    <td>~/.aws/credentials</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-red);">Critical — Cloud takeover</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>iCloud Keychain</td>
                    <td>~/Library/Keychains/</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-red);">Critical — All saved passwords</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Apple Notes</td>
                    <td>~/Library/Group Containers/</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-orange);">High — Often contains secrets</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Browser Data (Chrome/Safari)</td>
                    <td>Various</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-orange);">High — Session cookies, passwords</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>VPN Configs</td>
                    <td>~/Library/Application Support/</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-orange);">High — Corporate network access</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Crypto Wallets</td>
                    <td>Extension storage</td>
                    <td style="color: var(--accent-red);">Critical — Financial theft</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>Russian Locale Check</h3>
        <p>
            Notably, the malware <strong>avoids execution on machines with Russian locale settings</strong>.
            This is a common technique used by Russian-speaking cybercriminals to avoid prosecution under
            Russian law (which generally doesn't prosecute attacks against foreign targets).
        </p>

        <div class="technical-box">
            <pre><code class="language-javascript">// Locale check — won't execute on Russian systems

function shouldExecute() { const locale = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale; const timezone = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone;

if (locale.startsWith('ru') || timezone.includes('Moscow')) {
    return false; // Skip Russian systems
}
return true;

} 

        <h2 id="iocs"><i class="fas fa-biohazard"></i> Indicators of Compromise</h2>

        <h3>File Hashes (SHA-256)</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Hash</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>

        <h3>Network Indicators</h3>
        <ul>
            <li>api.mainnet-beta.solana.com (legitimate, used for C2 fetch)</li>
            <li>calendar.google.com (legitimate, used as fallback C2)</li>
            <li>Extension making unexpected Solana RPC calls</li>
        </ul>

        <div class="technical-box">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-shield-alt"></i> YARA Detection Rule</h3>
            <pre><code class="language-yara">rule GlassWorm_Wave2_2026 {
meta:
    description = "Detects GlassWorm Wave 2 VS Code extension malware"
    author = "TheHGTech Threat Research"
    date = "2026-02-03"
    
strings:
    // Unicode steganography markers
    $unicode_steg = { FE 00 FE 01 FE 02 FE 03 }
    
    // Solana C2 indicators
    $solana_rpc = "api.mainnet-beta.solana.com" ascii wide
    $solana_method = "getSignaturesForAddress" ascii wide
    
    // Credential theft paths (macOS)
    $ssh_path = ".ssh/" ascii wide
    $aws_creds = ".aws/credentials" ascii wide
    $keychain = "Keychains" ascii wide
    
    // Russian locale check
    $locale_check = /locale\.startsWith\(['"]ru['"]\)/ ascii wide
    $moscow_check = "Moscow" ascii wide
    
condition:
    (uint32(0) == 0x4B50) or // ZIP/VSIX magic
    (2 of ($solana_*) and any of ($ssh_path, $aws_creds, $keychain)) or
    ($unicode_steg and $locale_check)

} 

        <h2 id="mitigation"><i class="fas fa-shield-alt"></i> Defensive Actions</h2>

        <div class="success-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Immediate Recommendations</strong>
            <ol style="margin-top: 1rem;">
                <li><strong>Check Installed Extensions:</strong> Review for the four compromised extensions; remove
                    if present</li>
                <li><strong>Rotate Credentials:</strong> If compromised extensions were installed, rotate ALL
                    credentials: SSH, AWS, npm, GitHub</li>
                <li><strong>Enable Extension Signing:</strong> Where possible, only install signed extensions from
                    verified publishers</li>
                <li><strong>Monitor for Solana RPC:</strong> Alert on unexpected Solana blockchain API calls from
                    developer machines</li>
                <li><strong>macOS Hunt:</strong> Search for unexpected LaunchAgents and SOCKS proxy configurations
                </li>
            </ol>
        </div>

        <h3>Detection Script (macOS)</h3>
        <div class="technical-box">
            <pre><code class="language-bash">#!/bin/bash

GlassWorm Hunt Script for macOS

echo “🔍 Hunting for GlassWorm indicators…”

Check for suspicious LaunchAgents

echo -e “\n[1] Checking LaunchAgents…” ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E “update|sync|helper”

Check for unexpected SSH key access

echo -e “\n[2] Checking SSH directory access (last 7 days)…” find ~/.ssh -mtime -7 -type f 2>/dev/null

Check for SOCKS proxy

echo -e “\n[3] Checking for SOCKS proxy processes…” ps aux | grep -E “socks|proxy” | grep -v grep

Check VS Code extensions

echo -e “\n[4] Checking for compromised extensions…” EXTENSION_DIR=“$HOME/.vscode/extensions” for ext in “vscode-json-transform” “markdown-preview-enhanced-plus” “code-snippets-manager” “terminal-themes-collection”; do if [ -d “$EXTENSION_DIR”/“$ext” ] 2>/dev/null; then echo “⚠️ FOUND: $ext — REMOVE IMMEDIATELY” fi done

Check for Solana connections

echo -e “\n[5] Checking network connections to Solana…” netstat -an | grep -E “api.mainnet-beta.solana.com|8899”

echo -e “\n✅ Hunt complete. Review findings above.”
